text: A sharp-eyed reviewer noticed the Python outlier watchlist and the Power BI classification disagreed on about fourteen customers, all sitting right at the edge of the ninety-day line.
Isolating the mismatches shows every single one sits at exactly eighty-nine, ninety, or ninety-one days since last order — a dead giveaway that this is a boundary problem, not a logic problem.

First cause: the two sides were using different reference dates. The Power BI model's as-of date comes from the last scheduled refresh; the Python script's was pinned to a date run a day apart from that refresh.

Second cause, hiding inside Python alone: the main script correctly used 'days since last order, less than or equal to ninety' — but one ad hoc notebook cell, copy-pasted in a hurry, used a strict less-than instead.
Both get fixed: the as-of date now reads from the same shared value Power BI last refreshed against, and the ad hoc filter is corrected to match the main script's own boundary exactly.

Re-run against the identical date, and the fourteen mismatches disappear completely. The boundary convention gets written down explicitly, so the next script that reimplements this logic doesn't have to guess it. Next up: finally answering what this number means for the business.
